title: Introduction and lecture framing
groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

title: Principles of innate immune recognition
groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how innate immunity distinguishes danger through molecular patterns and appropriately positioned, germline-encoded receptors.

title: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into responses shaped by receptor location and cellular stress.

title: Non-TLR recognition pathways and inflammatory disease
groupedBecause: These subtopics show how danger-sensing pathways beyond toll-like receptors activate inflammation and can contribute to chronic inflammatory disease.

title: Sentinel-driven inflammation and leukocyte recruitment
groupedBecause: These subtopics follow the inflammatory response from sentinel-cell activation to the recruitment of circulating leukocytes into infected tissue.

title: Lymphatic transport and adaptive immune priming
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how drainage from infected tissues enables dendritic cells to initiate adaptive responses in lymph nodes.

title: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a life-threatening systemic response.

title: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation subsides through the changing balance between inflammatory stimulation and inhibitory signals.

title: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why inflamed tissue may recover or remain chronically inflamed when damaging triggers persist, with granulomas illustrating containment rather than clearance.

title: Lecture close and next lecture
groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next lecture.
